title: Intercession
lead: Praying on behalf of others. Abraham pleads for Sodom (Genesis 18), Moses for Israel after the golden calf (Exodus 32–34; Numbers 14), Samuel, Jeremiah and Daniel for their people, and the New Testament presents Christ and the Spirit as intercessors (Romans 8:26–34; Hebrews 7:25).

sections.b: Abraham bargains with God for Sodom (Genesis 18:22–33) and prays for Abimelech (Genesis 20:7, 17). Moses pleads after the calf (Exodus 32–34) and again after the spies (Numbers 14:13–20), and Aaron runs with incense between the living and the dead (Numbers 16:46–48). Samuel says it would be a sin for him to stop praying for Israel (1 Samuel 12:23). God tells Jeremiah not to pray for the people and says that even Moses and Samuel could not turn him now (Jeremiah 7:16; 15:1). Ezekiel finds no one to stand in the gap (Ezekiel 22:30), and Daniel confesses his people's sins (Daniel 9). Jesus prays for his disciples (John 17), the Spirit pleads for believers (Romans 8:26–27), and the risen Christ lives to intercede for them (Romans 8:34; Hebrews 7:25).
